analyticCertificate: Near x=1 the integrand has a nonzero simple-pole residue, so the two one-sided improper integrals diverge.
For the principal value put t=x^q, then split at one and substitute t=1/u on the upper piece.
The combined integrable expression is q^-1 integral_0^1 (u^(p/q-1)-u^(-p/q))/(1-u) du.

The digamma reflection identity gives pi cot(pi p/q)/q. Under symmetric x cutoffs 1 plus/minus delta, the transformed cutoff ratio ((1+delta)^q-1)/(1-(1-delta)^q) tends to one; the possible logarithmic correction therefore vanishes.
assumptions: 0<p<q; p/q!=1/2 in this asset; PV uses symmetric x cutoffs at the sole pole x=1.

pedagogy.difficultyRationale: The ordinary integral and symmetric principal value have different existence conclusions; a transformed cutoff correction must be controlled. Solve-time and difficulty estimates are editorial, not measured player calibration.

solutionSteps: \text{The ordinary integral diverges because each one-sided integral at the pole diverges.}
\text{For symmetric cutoffs at the original pole, the transformed cutoff ratio tends to one.}
\text{In the upper piece use }u=1/t\text{; combine both pieces on }(0,1).
\text{This is the digamma reflection identity, equivalently its convergent difference series.}
\textnormal{In the common form used by the choices, the result is}
statement: \textnormal{For }I=\int_0^\infty\frac{x^{4}}{1-x^{11}}\,\mathrm{d}x\textnormal{, choose the pair (ordinary integral, Cauchy principal value at }x=1\textnormal{).}

analyticCertificate: Near x=1 the integrand has a nonzero simple-pole residue, so the two one-sided improper integrals diverge.
For the principal value put t=x^q, then split at one and substitute t=1/u on the upper piece.
The combined integrable expression is q^-1 integral_0^1 (u^(p/q-1)-u^(-p/q))/(1-u) du.

The digamma reflection identity gives pi cot(pi p/q)/q. Under symmetric x cutoffs 1 plus/minus delta, the transformed cutoff ratio ((1+delta)^q-1)/(1-(1-delta)^q) tends to one; the possible logarithmic correction therefore vanishes.
assumptions: 0<p<q; p/q!=1/2 in this asset; PV uses symmetric x cutoffs at the sole pole x=1.
